newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO says Israel fights Arafat, not violence.
newsitem.headline: PLO says Israel fights Arafat, not violence.

text.p: A senior Palestinian minister hit back at Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday, saying the PLO had acted to prevent violence but that Israel's right-wing government had done its best to scrap peace.
"During the recent months and weeks, we have prevented many incidents and terrorist acts to ensure security and peace," Information Minister Yasser Abed Rabbo told reporters in self-ruled Ramallah.
"But Netanyahu was exerting maximum effort to demolish Palestinian houses, build settlements and undermine peace."
Abed Rabbo was speaking two days after two Arab suicide bombers killed 13 people in an Israeli market.

Netanyahu, who became prime minister last year on a pledge to bring Israelis peace and security, has accused Palestinian President Yasser Arafat of doing "damn all" to control militants in areas under his authority.
"I am ready to appear on television to show the people that while Arafat was fighting violence, Netanyahu was stabbing him in the back," Abed Rabbo said.
"American and Israeli security officials have proof of PLO measures to combat violence," he said.

After Wednesday's bombings, Israel suspended peace talks with the Palestinians, imposed a total closure on the West Bank and Gaza Strip and threatened that its army would re-enter PLO-ruled areas to arrest militants if Arafat failed to act.
PLO officials said Arafat considered the Israeli measures "dangerous steps" and demanded immediate international intervention to prevent moves that would lead to violence.
Abed Rabbo said Netanyahu's policies were "aimed at weakening Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat and his Authority rather than aimed at fighting terrorism."

Calling Netanyahu's decisions after the bombings "unwise", Abed Rabbo said it was "ironic" that Netanyahu was demanding that the Palestinian leader undertake strict security measures to prevent violence while simultaneously weakening him.

"Security requires implementing strict security measures and a wise political leadership. We have done our best to guarantee the former but it is up to the Israeli people to secure a wise political leadership."
"Even the strictest security measures would fail to guarantee security if the leadership was unwise."
PLO officials have condemned Wednesday's bombings.
A leaflet in the name of the Islamic Movement Hamas claimed responsibility for the attacks but Israeli and PLO officials questioned its authenticity.
Hamas has stood behind many suicide bombings that killed scores in Israel since the signing of a 1993 PLO-Israel interim peace accord.

Senior PLO official Mahmoud Abbas said Israel's blockade of the West Bank and Gaza increased despair among Palestinians and fed extremism. Abed Rabbo called the closure a "racist collective punishment never practiced in any civilised state on earth."
Abbas said bilateral security coordination resumed after Wednesday's bombings. Israeli and PLO forces each made arrests in areas under their control after the bombings.
PLO-Israeli security cooperation and peace talks were suspended in March after Israel began building a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
